title: Who owns the shared skill library
caption: Shared, general skills need rules for who adds, checks and removes them, and there is no settled practice yet.
analogy: The fleet manual's front page. Fleet, ship and project are the tiers; the robots are the models and agents.

add.chat: The organisation's library is set to “Requires review”, “Open” or “Off”; a reviewer approves a fixed version.
add.coding: Whoever can merge to the repository; for plugins, admins choose which marketplaces and plugins are allowed and enabled.

tier.chat: Personal, shared, plugin or organisation-wide; only owners add or remove at the top tier.
tier.coding: ~/.claude/skills/ you, in every project · .claude/skills/ the repository · a plugin or managed settings: a whole team.

cost.chat: A loaded skill is a recurring token cost.
cost.coding: The loaded SKILL.md stays in the context window: a recurring token cost.

models.term: Which models and agents it works with
models.chat: A skill's value depends on the model and the agent it runs in.
models.coding: Tested in the agent it ships to: the same model in another harness can turn a skill's effect around.

retire.chat: Deprecate it when its evals keep failing or its workflow is retired.
retire.coding: Pin production skills to a version; deprecate when evals consistently fail.

inset.heading: SKILL.md, its metadata map
inset.note: The Agent Skills format has no owner field; these keys are a convention.

darkCorner: Not settled yet: no common practice so far.

footer.chat: Fleet, ship and project are this Episode's words, not vendor terms: vendors tier skills by audience and risk, not by how general the content is.
footer.coding: Codex splits repository skill folders from user skill folders the same way Claude Code does.

alt.scene: Midnight water, the robot hanging on its cable with its lamp lit. Left, the shared, general square of Slide 18's skill scope matrix, ringed, with a small locator showing where it sits among the four. A beam of light opens that square into the shared skill library's front page, drawn as the fleet manual on its binder: who may add a skill, whom it reaches, what it costs to load, which models and agents it works with, and when it retires. The page's lower corner is dark: not settled yet.

shared-skills-are-tiered-by-audience.header: Shared skills are tiered by audience
shared-skills-are-tiered-by-audience.description: Anthropic's tiers in claude.ai: personal skills, skills shared with individuals, group skills bundled in a plugin, and organisation-wide skills that only owners can add or remove [1]. "Fleet, ship, project" are the Episode's words, not vendor terms; vendors tier by audience and risk, not by how general the content is.

anthropic-provision-and-manage-skills.title: Anthropic, Provision and manage skills for your organization

who-adds-reviews-and-removes-shared-skil.header: Who adds, reviews and removes shared skills
who-adds-reviews-and-removes-shared-skil.description: the org library offers "Requires review", "Open" and "Off", a reviewer approves "a fixed version" and users stay on it until a new one is approved [1]. Anthropic says to pin production skills to a version and to deprecate skills whose evaluations consistently fail or whose workflow is retired [2].

token-cost-and-model-fit-are-per-skill-f.description: a loaded skill is a recurring token cost [1], and a skill's value depends on the model and harness it runs in [2].

claude-code-skills.title: Anthropic, Extend Claude with skills (Claude Code documentation)

swe-skills-bench.title: Han et al., SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?

skill-governance-still-being-worked-out-.header: Skill governance "still being worked out" is a judgement
skill-governance-still-being-worked-out-.description: Anthropic's enterprise guidance lists what to track per skill (purpose, owner, version, evaluation status) and does not report how many organisations do so [1], so the unsettled corner is the Episode's judgement, not a measured claim.

back-to-the-square.title: Back to the square
back-to-the-square.script: Come back to the matrix, to the shared, general square. That is the kind of skill the most people rely on, so it is where care matters most.

what-the-front-page-needs.title: What the front page needs
what-the-front-page-needs.script: A shared library needs rules beyond the owner and the version: who may add a skill, which tier it sits in and so whom it reaches, what it costs to load, which models and agents it works with, and when it retires. Each is a question somebody has to answer before the skill goes in.

the-dark-corner.title: The dark corner
the-dark-corner.script: And then there are the questions nobody has settled yet. I want to be plain with you: I do not have the answers there, and I don't think many organisations do yet. If you have worked it out in yours, I would like to hear how.
